item.title: Every New Open-World RPG Of This Year, Officially Ranked
item.description:
2026 has already been a pretty great year for open-world RPGs , with several promising upcoming titles also scheduled for the fall season. From long-awaited sequels and free-to-play releases to faithful remakes and brand-new IPs with potentially bright futures, fans of the genre already have their hands pretty full. Some might even need extra time in 2027 to finish everything released this year.

While it is pretty much impossible to count “every” new open-world RPG released in 2026 so far, this list will focus exclusively on major titles that made a noticeable impact, with no early access games included. Also, while critic and player scores contribute to the “official” ranking, they aren’t definitive, so some games may rank higher or lower based on my personal judgment. Even with these rules, there are plenty of interesting and varied titles to cover, so let’s just get into it.

“Where’s Crimson Desert?”

One thing that needs clarification is the ongoing debate over whether Crimson Desert belongs to the RPG genre. Pearl Abyss specifically calls it an action-adventure rather than a full-fledged RPG, and it’s easy to see why. The game places a strong emphasis on puzzles and traversal mechanics, features non-traditional combat scenarios such as clearing waves of respawning enemies in camps and fortresses, and offers relatively light skill trees, little build variety, and almost no branching quests or ways to influence the story. Crimson Desert is at its best as an open-world adventure with tremendous freedom of exploration. Still, if you are convinced it belongs in this ranking, it would probably land somewhere in the Top-3 games here.

8 The Division Resurgence

It’s Like the Successor, but Backwards

  • Global Steam Reviews: 47% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 75

More of an honorable mention, Tom Clancy’s The Division Resurgence was originally developed for mobile and later ported to PC. It is unlikely to impress the series’ hardcore fans unless they have completely run out of content in the previous installments. The game often feels like a watered-down version of The Division 2 , which becomes especially apparent when compared to the latter’s more than seven years of active support, with Ubisoft still showing no signs of stopping.

8 New Open-World RPGs Officially Confirmed For Next Year

As the open-world RPG genre continues to be bigger than ever, these massive games are slated for 2027.

1
By Vlad Mazanko

Still, for casual players looking for a decent tactical looter shooter, The Division Resurgence could be worth trying, especially since it is free-to-play and retains much of the series’ signature DNA. Naturally, you’d better be prepared for a heavy grind and considerably less content variety than its predecessors offer.

7 The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin

Falling Into the Same Old Traps

  • Global Steam Reviews: 60% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 70

Despite its intriguing premise, apparent ambition, and richly realized world of Britannia, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin ultimately disappoints, falling into largely the same familiar traps associated with free-to-play titles built around gacha mechanics. Overall, the game simply feels too heavily inspired by Genshin Impact , which is unsurprising but ultimately holds it back.

From excessively gated progression and repetitive quests and activities to a weak endgame and an underutilized setting, the game never seems to fully realize its potential. On top of that, it suffers from persistent technical issues and general jank. There’s still some fun to be had in Britannia, especially during the initial hours filled with discovery, but ultimately, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is among the least essential titles of the year in this segment.

6 Code Vein 2

One Step Forward, Two Steps Back

  • Global Steam Reviews: 65% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 73

Arriving many years after the original, Code Vein 2 is another title that leaves a bitter taste in one’s mouth, especially when thinking about “what could’ve been” or comparing it to other soulslikes released in 2026. Unlike most games here, the sequel’s biggest sin is probably its decision to go fully open-world, resulting in a poorly realized, bloated, and repetitive playground that only dilutes the package’s strongest pillars. The uneven world design and limited variety in enemies, environments, and even bosses cause fatigue to set in long before the ending.

5 Open-World RPGs Everyone Should Play To Completion

Nobody needs to complete every open-world RPG, but everyone should try to complete these open-world RPGs.

By Mark Sammut

Still, Code Vein 2 notably improves upon the original mechanically, offering better combat options and making it much easier to experiment with a greater variety of builds. Its more flexible design also makes the game approachable, as there are always new directions to explore instead of getting stuck on a single obstacle.

Nioh 3 is excluded from this list because the developers specifically describe it as an “open-field,” interconnected zone-based game rather than a full open-world like Rise of the Ronin .

5 NTE: Neverness to Everness

A Wee Bit Away From Becoming the Benchmark

  • Global Steam Reviews: 83% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 71

Anime-style visuals are all but dominant in the free-to-play gaming segment, but fortunately for NTE: Neverness to Everness , its fresh urban aesthetic helps it stand out from a myriad of similar fantasy titles. Coupled with a rich supernatural layer, the game delivers a genuinely memorable experience, where investigating twisted paranormal events and chasing otherworldly beings as Anomaly Hunters called Appraisers can easily carry the entire adventure.

Neverness to Everness seemingly tries to be too many things at once, including a city life simulator and management sandbox, yet it proves surprisingly competent at nearly all of them. Packed with activities and robust progression mechanics, the game’s unique design choices and memorable soundtrack grant it a distinct personality more than anything else. With some dedication and greater attention paid to its narrative layer, NTE could really evolve into one of the genre’s benchmarks.

4 Gothic 1 Remake

Stepping Into the Time Machine

  • Global Steam Reviews: 88% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 73

Gothic 1 Remake easily claims the title of the most faithful RPG remake in quite some time, offering a ticket back to an era when the genre felt radically different from its modern-day incarnation. Tough, compact, challenging, and absolutely brutal, Gothic makes you fight for every inch, with nothing handed to you without a struggle. Its world and inhabitants truly feel alive, resulting in a deeply personal and immersive experience.

6 Long Action RPGs That Take Forever To Complete, Ranked

From classic combat-focused narrative-driven RPGs to ARPGs that you can play endlessly, every title here is merciless with your free time.

4
By Vlad Mazanko

Alkimia Interactive really did the classic justice, modernizing only the parts that needed it while respecting all the signature features that make Piranha Bytes games so special. Gothic 1 Remake is demanding but rewarding, and all your choices, discoveries, victories, and defeats stay with you. Sure, some jank is unavoidable here, which makes the game a tough sell for modern players looking for AAA levels of polish.

3 DragonSword: Awakening

Hitting Way Above Expectations

  • Global Steam Reviews: 89% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 87

One of the unexpected favorites among 2026’s open-world RPGs, DragonSword: Awakening has turned out to be a really pleasant surprise. The game delivers a colorful open world across the Continent of Orbis that is fun to explore, while its flashy tag-team combat remains accessible yet deep enough to experiment with and gradually master. There are even some Pokemon-esque elements in the mix, with collectible companions called Familiars aiding you on your journey.

DragonSword: Awakening’s strengths are undeniable, and it essentially feels like Genshin Impact without gacha. Even so, it might not suit players looking for stronger narrative hooks due to its fairly generic central premise of stopping a reawakened dragon, while its anime-style presentation might not appeal to everyone, either. While it’s a pleasant experience overall, it hardly brings enough new ideas to the genre to be cherished for years to come. Still, in the grand scheme of things, these shortcomings are little more than nitpicks in what remains one of the year’s most pleasant surprises.

2 Mortal Shell 2

Undeniable Growth. Still Too Little Color

  • Global Steam Reviews: 77% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 85

One of the standout open-world action RPGs of the year so far, Mortal Shell 2 isn’t perfect, but it confidently nails most of the essentials. A noticeable step up from the original in every department, it is a true hard-rock sequel with an atmospheric, bleak world that feels fragmented yet connected at all times. The opening hours leave you completely lost in the best possible sense, with paths branching at every turn as you desperately try to navigate toward the next save beacon.

5 Near-Perfect Turn-Based RPGS Nobody Played

Turn-based RPGs were huge once upon a time, but some truly great games never got the love and attention they deserve.

4
By Mark Sammut

With a tighter combat system, genuinely distinct Shells serving as flexible classes, refined visuals, deep lore infused with cosmic horror, and plenty of optional dungeons and secrets, Mortal Shell 2 offers a brutal 50-hour gauntlet that tests fans of the genre in every way imaginable. Some technical caveats may spoil the early impression for certain players, yet it’s safe to assume that Mortal Shell 2 has already cemented its place as a must-play modern soulslike.

1 The Blood of Dawnwalker

The Birth of a Promising New RPG Franchise

  • Global Steam Reviews: 80% Positive
  • OpenCritic Average: 85

Easily among the most anticipated open-world RPGs of 2026, The Blood of Dawnwalker appears to have proved that the wait was worth it, delivering a solid first chapter for Rebel Wolves’ planned vampire saga. Strong early critical reception (although not everyone is fully sold) highlights Dawnwalker’s greatest strengths, including its thick atmosphere, excellent worldbuilding, and dark, mature themes. Meanwhile, unique features such as time constraints, complete nonlinearity, and a half-vampire protagonist set it apart from almost everything we’ve seen in the genre recently.

Judging by the first wave of player feedback, many have greatly enjoyed The Blood of Dawnwalker , with most caveats involving technical issues that will likely be ironed out after launch. As it stands, this is an undeniably strong debut, filled with everything we love RPGs for, and one of 2026’s strongest offerings. It should only become better after several months of patches and refinements, and it’s already exciting to see where the team goes from here.

Every New Open-World RPG Of This Year, Officially Ranked

5 Open-World RPGs With The Most Unique Class Systems
6 Near-Perfect Open-World Games Nobody Wanted

item.title: Best Teams for Centers in MyCareer in NBA 2K27
item.description:
When choosing a team for Centers in NBA 2K27's MyCareer, players will want to look out for rosters that lack a star big man at the 5, allowing them an early chance at starting. However, the team would ideally have talent in other positions, such as an elite Point Guard to play the pick-and-roll with and some shooters to stretch the floor. The following teams are some great options for Centers at the start of the upcoming 2026/27 season of the NBA, as well as historical rosters from across five eras.

Best Teams for Point Guards in MyCareer in NBA 2K27

For a few seasons, the Orlando Magic have been one of the most exciting young teams, slowly building momentum led by All-Star Paulo Banchero and Franz Wagner. However, with injuries and the lack of a star Center, the Magic have failed to make that next jump in the postseason. This is where MP comes in, completing this young roster, with Jalen Suggs and Desmond Bane also being great players in the backcourt. Any style of play would help this team compete in the East that has surely gotten stronger in the off-season.

However, with Darius Garland, who formerly had regular-season success with the Cavs, and MP as a star Center for the Clippers, it's quite possible for the former champ to once again compete at the top. The Clippers' current starting Center is the 38-year-old Brook Lopez, who is far past his prime, giving MP an easy route into the starting five.

After many seasons without hope and their New York rivals recently winning it all, the Brooklyn Nets could do with some help from MP. While they have Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle, they need a young star to build around. This would be the perfect destination for an all-around Center who can score, pass, and defend, as the Nets need everything. Aside from their two best players, the rest of the roster is very young, meaning they could start competing in a season or two. The Nets also have an abundance of picks for future drafts. All of this could make for a more realistic career mode experience, especially for those not wanting to spend money on VC to become an instant All-Star.

Best Historic MyCareer Teams For Centers In NBA 2K27

For the first time ever in the NBA 2K series, players can experience MyCareer in one of five historic eras stretching back to the 1980's. There is no story like Fire & Concrete, but with retro graphics, old-school jerseys, and historical rosters, the immersion is unmatched. Players simply choose any NBA team from one of these eras and instantly become a starter at the Center position.

The available eras are as follows:

  • The Magic vs. Bird Era: Begins in 1984.
  • The Jordan Era: Begins in 1991.
  • The Kobe Era: Begins in 2003.
  • The LeBron Era: Begins in 2010.
  • The Steph Era: Begins in 2016.

Below are some interesting historical teams to join as a C enter in MyCareer Eras .

  • Golden State Warriors: Help Steph Curry reach greatness early

The Steph Era - 2016

  • Cleveland Cavaliers: Make LeBron's and Kyrie's Cavs invincible alongside Kevin Love

  • Houston Rockets: Pair up with prime James Harden
  • Phoenix Suns: Rise with a young Devin Booker

  • Golden State Warriors: Center is the only missing piece for an unbeatable team

item.title: New Roguelike Deckbuilder on Steam Is Already One of the Best Games I've Played All Year
item.description:
I love roguelikes, simply for the fact that I find their risk-reward loop immensely satisfying. However, I haven't played too many deckbuilding roguelikes, not because they don't interest me, but because my backlog generally has me drifting toward something else instead. And yet, after spending over an hour with Shroom and Gloom 's demo on Steam , it's officially on the list of games I plan to prioritize this September—which is saying a lot already, considering how stacked this month really is. To be quite honest, I could have invested a lot more time into Shroom and Gloom 's demo, as it's incredibly generous with what it offers, and I simply couldn't get enough of what I played. While I haven't played the full game just yet since it launches on September 10, 2026, I can confidently say that if it's anything like the demo, it will be, without a doubt, one of the best roguelike deckbuilders out there. I'm certain of it.

Shroom and Gloom separates itself from your traditional roguelike deckbuilder in many ways, but its standout feature is that it plays more like a first-person 3D dungeon crawler with a roguelike deckbuilding loop built in, which makes it far more immersive than most of the games I've played in the genre. That's far from its only distinguishing characteristic, though. In fact, it's probably more accurate to call it a roguelike double-deckbuilder because you get to manage two decks throughout the game. More on that later, but I'll say right out of the gate that it makes building your decks all the more rewarding, considering each deck is used for completely different purposes. Throw in one of the most captivating art styles I've ever seen in a game like this, as well as an unforgettable atmosphere, some sharp humor, and just the right amount of weirdness, and Shroom the Gloom becomes what I can't help but label one of the most promising indie titles I've played on Steam in a long time.

New Action RPG on Steam is Basically Diablo With a Unique Ghost of Tsushima Twist

An upcoming action RPG on Steam gives an Eastern fantasy twist on the classic Diablo formula (with a touch of Ghost of Tsushima).

1
By Joshua Duckworth

Shroom and Gloom Had Me Hooked Almost Immediately

Check Out Shroom and Gloom's Demo on Steam

Before I even launched the demo for Shroom and Gloom , I was already intrigued by the fact that this short little taste of the game alone had already managed to achieve an Overwhelmingly Positive rating on Steam. For a roguelike deckbuilder, that's already pretty significant, though the genre's fanbase has grown tremendously over the last few years. But the reason that's such a big deal is because, at some point, I feel like it's all the same. I mean... how much can you actually do with this formula that makes it considerably different from any other game in the genre? As it turns out, I think Shroom and Gloom may have found a little niche to carve itself into, and I can't wait for all the other games that will likely draw inspiration from it if it succeeds.

Wishlist Today

For me, that opinion started forming as soon as I started a new run in the demo. I was dropped into this dark yet colorful world, where I could see my hand in front of me holding up a piece of paper with a solitary "W" on it, clearly telling me to... walk? This is something I wasn't yet familiar with in the realm of roguelike deckbuilders, so I just stood there motionless for a second, even attempting to click on the paper thinking it would do something. But when I finally hit the W key on my keyboard and started moving, the beautiful, strange environment before me began unraveling, and I was instantly smitten with Shroom and Gloom .

I think Shroom and Gloom may have found a little niche to carve itself into, and I can't wait for all the other games that will likely draw inspiration from it if it succeeds.

Moving forward just a little more, I found a shovel wedged into the ground, so I picked it up and it became a card. Then, just ahead, a black "X" appeared on the ground, and since, as they say, "X marks the spot," I clicked and dragged my shovel card to that spot, unearthing a key card that I could use on the locked door in front of me. Walking through the door, I entered a dark stairwell that led me deep into an even darker room, where cards for a rusted hammer and a matchstick appeared in my hands.

With the matchstick, I lit a torch in front of me that I could barely see, and the room lit up. The rusted hammer, on the other hand, I could use to break the lock on yet another locked door. On the other side, another stairwell, but one where the bones of a poor soul who had lost their way clutched a backpack that contained the first few cards of my Explore deck. But beyond the locked door in front of me, which I would unlock with a key I found in the backpack, lay my first battle with Shroom and Gloom 's strange (but also kind of adorable) enemies, where my entirely separate combat deck appeared in my hands. At that point, I had realized just how special this game is, and I wanted to keep going, wherever it would take me.

Shroom and Gloom's Double-Deckbuilding Makes Its Roguelike Loop Doubly Satisfying

Without a doubt, one of Shroom and Gloom 's best qualities is its double-deckbuilding loop, particularly with how seamlessly it works with its first-person dungeon crawling experience. Essentially, you have one deck that is used for camp and exploration and a separate deck that is used for combat. The Explore deck is what you'll have in your hands while you're making your way through the dungeon, and its cards can be used to interact with the world, modify other cards, and unlock new weapons and abilities. Then, when you walk into a room with enemies, that deck disappears and your Combat deck takes its place. Once the fight is over, you're right back to exploring again, and it doesn't take long before you're bouncing between both decks so often that they start to feel like two halves of the same loop.

The Explore deck is probably what surprised me the most, simply because I expected most of the actual deckbuilding to happen in combat. Instead, Shroom and Gloom gives you cards for things you would normally just do with the press of a button in any other first-person dungeon crawler. That shovel I mentioned earlier is one example, since I could use it to dig up whatever was buried beneath those black Xs I found along the way, but there are plenty of other ways these cards come into play as you move deeper into the dungeon. Better yet, exploration is also where you can find opportunities to improve the cards you already have, so I'm not simply walking from one battle to another while waiting for the "real" game to start again. I'm still building my run in between fights, only now I'm doing it while physically moving through this strange underground world and wondering what might be behind the next door.

Shroom and Gloom's Combat Is All About Ridiculous Cards and Eating Your Enemies

Then there are the battles themselves, which are where Shroom and Gloom starts showing just how ridiculous it is willing to let things get. Like most deckbuilders, each turn gives you a hand of cards to work with, and you're trying to figure out the best way to use what you've been dealt before handing things over to the enemy. But the real fun comes from what happens to those cards as the run progresses, because Shroom and Gloom lets you continue growing and modifying them until something that started out fairly harmless can become absolutely absurd. During my time with the demo, I was already starting to see how quickly one good card could turn into the centerpiece of an entire build, and once that starts happening, every opportunity to improve it becomes increasingly hard to pass up.

Shroom and Gloom also has a pretty hilarious solution for staying alive that fits this entire game far better than a traditional healing potion ever could. Rather than relying heavily on blocking damage, you're encouraged to cook and eat the mushrooms trying to kill you. Depending on the cards you have, you can season them, roast them, and eventually gobble them up to recover lost health. You can even toss roasted enemies into a pot and turn them into soup, which can provide additional benefits. Again, this is a game where I had already used a shovel card to dig up a key and a matchstick card to light a torch, so when I was encouraged to start preparing my enemies for dinner, I was more than happy to go along with it.

Without a doubt, one of Shroom and Gloom 's best qualities is its double-deckbuilding loop, particularly with how seamlessly it works with its first-person dungeon crawling experience.

And this is basically how a run keeps pulling you forward. You'll make your way deeper into the dungeon, use your Explore deck to deal with whatever you find along the way, stumble into another battle, build up your Combat deck, and then head right back out to see what else is waiting for you. Meanwhile, both decks are constantly changing as you find new cards and improve the ones you already have, so there was almost always something I wanted to do before I stopped playing. Maybe I wanted to see what was through one more door. Maybe I had just improved a card and wanted to see what it could do in the next fight. Or maybe I had found the beginnings of some stupidly powerful combo and wanted to know just how far I could take it before the run came crashing down.

Of course, it eventually will come crashing down because this is still a roguelike, and dying means starting over. But even then, the demo has Foresight cards that can shape future runs, which gives you another reason to jump back in rather than feeling like everything you just did was wasted. And considering the demo alone has 26 handcrafted tunnels to fight your way through, I constantly felt like there was still something I hadn't seen yet. I originally went into Shroom and Gloom expecting to play long enough to understand what it was all about, capture some footage, and move on. Instead, I kept telling myself I would stop after the next fight, then the next room, then the next upgrade, until I finally looked at the clock and realized more than an hour had just vanished. That, to me, is when you know it's a good roguelike.

New Stardew Valley Meets Undertale Life Sim on Steam Went Somewhere I Never Saw Coming
New Elden Ring Meets Dishonored Action RPG on Steam Just Sold Me on First-Person Soulslikes
New Stardew Valley Meets How to Train Your Dragon Game on Steam Left Me Hungry for More

But if Shroom and Gloom 's full release can keep building on what its demo already does this well, I have a feeling I'm going to lose a lot more than an hour to it when it launches on September 10, 2026. There are still plenty of cards I haven't seen, combinations I haven't tried, and probably more bizarre ways to interact with its weird world than I'm even aware of yet, which is more than enough to have me counting down the days. September is already packed with games I want to play, but Shroom and Gloom has somehow worked its way near the top of that list, and after what I played in the demo, I don't see it getting knocked down anytime soon.

Shroom and Gloom

item.title: Upcoming Battlefield 6 Crossover Leaks Online
item.description:
Battlefield 6 may be collaborating with Dead Space for an upcoming Halloween event, according to a recent leak. EA's popular large-scale first-person shooter has been going strong, bringing a steady stream of content for both its base multiplayer experience and standalone battle royale mode, REDSEC . While the game is still receiving improvements, some players are happy with all the game has to offer so far. However, it looks like Battlefield 6 may be gearing up for a horror-fueled update this fall.

The title has collaborated with other franchises before, as Battlefield 6 previously featured a crossover with Top Gun during Season 4 in August 2026. Gaming hardware manufacturer Razer also teamed up with the action-packed shooter for the game's launch, giving players the opportunity to earn an exclusive skin as a promotional reward. While Battlefield 6 's crossovers and cosmetics have remained grounded for the most part, a potential joint project with Dead Space looks to be on the cards heading into Season 5.

Steam Refunds Player With 470 Hours in Battlefield 6

According to a recent Reddit post, one Battlefield 6 player with 470 hours in the game has just been given a full refund on Steam.

By Cameron Swan

Battlefield 6 Leak Points to a Dead Space Crossover

Credible dataminer and leaker Temporyal recently shared details on Twitter revealing that Battlefield 6 could receive two Dead Space crossover skins. These skins are part of 36 total unreleased cosmetics, presented among a mixture of MilSim soldier uniforms. According to Temporyal, the skins are set to debut alongside a larger Halloween event for the Season 5 update , slated to arrive in Winter 2026. This would not be the first time that the two franchises have collided, as Battlefield 2042 also received a Dead Space collaboration in 2024 for its own special event titled “Outbreak.”

These leaked cosmetics also feature a Medal of Honor -themed soldier, another popular Electronic Arts IP. Temporyal went on to reveal that an Area 51 map will debut for the update, where players must "prevent the end of the world." These uncovered skins and details also align with leaked footage provided by Twitter user Oyrcs, who showcased Battlefield 6 gameplay of the Dead Space Pulse Rifle. This item is set to be featured as a Battle Pickup and will likely play a role in the upcoming event.

While Dead Space has crossed over with series before, some avid players are voicing their concerns over the game moving away from its traditional grounded military-themed presentation and updates. Whether the franchise should feature cosmetics that do not align with the game's overall art style and theme has long been a heated topic of discussion among the Battlefield community, with some players falling on one side, while others are calling for more creative additions that do not stick true to the standard MilSim experience.

If Battlefield 6 somehow tops the franchise's last partnership with the terrifying horror game, it may just be a hit.

Battlefield 6 may be collaborating with Dead Space for an upcoming Halloween event, according to a recent leak. EA's popular large-scale first-person shooter has been going strong, bringing a steady stream of content for both its base multiplayer experience and standalone battle royale mode, REDSEC . While the game is still receiving improvements, some players are happy with all the game has to offer so far. However, it looks like Battlefield 6 may be gearing up for a horror-fueled update this fall.

The title has collaborated with other franchises before, as Battlefield 6 previously featured a crossover with Top Gun during Season 4 in August 2026. Gaming hardware manufacturer Razer also teamed up with the action-packed shooter for the game's launch, giving players the opportunity to earn an exclusive skin as a promotional reward. While Battlefield 6 's crossovers and cosmetics have remained grounded for the most part, a potential joint project with Dead Space looks to be on the cards heading into Season 5.

Steam Refunds Player With 470 Hours in Battlefield 6

According to a recent Reddit post, one Battlefield 6 player with 470 hours in the game has just been given a full refund on Steam.

By Cameron Swan

Battlefield 6 Leak Points to a Dead Space Crossover

Credible dataminer and leaker Temporyal recently shared details on Twitter revealing that Battlefield 6 could receive two Dead Space crossover skins. These skins are part of 36 total unreleased cosmetics, presented among a mixture of MilSim soldier uniforms. According to Temporyal, the skins are set to debut alongside a larger Halloween event for the Season 5 update , slated to arrive in Winter 2026. This would not be the first time that the two franchises have collided, as Battlefield 2042 also received a Dead Space collaboration in 2024 for its own special event titled “Outbreak.”

These leaked cosmetics also feature a Medal of Honor -themed soldier, another popular Electronic Arts IP. Temporyal went on to reveal that an Area 51 map will debut for the update, where players must "prevent the end of the world." These uncovered skins and details also align with leaked footage provided by Twitter user Oyrcs, who showcased Battlefield 6 gameplay of the Dead Space Pulse Rifle. This item is set to be featured as a Battle Pickup and will likely play a role in the upcoming event.

While Dead Space has crossed over with series before, some avid players are voicing their concerns over the game moving away from its traditional grounded military-themed presentation and updates. Whether the franchise should feature cosmetics that do not align with the game's overall art style and theme has long been a heated topic of discussion among the Battlefield community, with some players falling on one side, while others are calling for more creative additions that do not stick true to the standard MilSim experience.

If Battlefield 6 somehow tops the franchise's last partnership with the terrifying horror game, it may just be a hit.

item.title: Steam Users Can Claim a 10/10 Masterpiece Completely Free of Charge on September 9
item.description:
Steam users will have the opportunity to claim a free key for the first season of Telltale's The Walking Dead on September 9. This free Steam giveaway has been announced ahead of time, but it will be available only while keys last, so it's first-come, first-served to pick up this 2012 masterpiece.

Telltale's The Walking Dead Season 1 was released in 2012 to massive critical acclaim. Its narrative remains one of the best Walking Dead stories to date, and the game helped to revitalize the struggling adventure game genre. Player choice was central to the experience, carrying through to later seasons in a way that truly mattered. Players were responsible for which characters lived and died, and they would live with those choices throughout their entire playthrough. Even 14 years later, it's a remarkable adventure game, one that is well worth playing, free or not.

Here's Every Walking Dead Game You Can Play Before Dead City Season 3 Gets Here

Dead City Season 3 arrives on July 26, so that gives you time to play through a bunch of Walking Dead games.

By Mark Sammut

The Walking Dead Season 1 is Free to Keep on September 9

  • Claim The Walking Dead via Lenovo Gaming Community Drops
  • Giveaway starts at 12 PM ET on September 9

On September 9 at 12 PM ET, Steam users will be able to claim a free copy of Telltale's 10/10 masterpiece, The Walking Dead , via a new Lenovo Gaming Community Key Drop event. This giveaway will only snag gamers the first season, but given the fact that it's commonly considered to be among the best choice-based games of all time, it's hard to complain when it's 100% free. Users need to sign up for the Lenovo Gaming Community to claim this giveaway, which will be available only while keys remain. Being in the queue does not guarantee a key, so it's worth jumping in as close to the start time as possible.

Free Game Giveaways

AllEnding SoonSteamEpicPrimePSNItch

Free Game Giveaways

This free Steam Walking Dead giveaway was initially planned for August 19, but was delayed shortly after starting due to technical issues. Not only has Lenovo set a new date, but it also says it made backend changes to its Key Drop system that should make the process "much faster and more stable for users." It's an excellent initiative, so hopefully, this time the giveaway goes without a hitch.

  1. Have valid accounts on Steam, Twitch, and the Legion Gaming Community
  2. Refresh the key page linked above at the start time (12 PM ET, September 9, 2026) to join the queue
  3. Complete Steam and Twitch account confirmation steps on Gleam
  4. Link Lenovo Gaming community account in Gleam

While The Walking Dead remains popular, it is perhaps not the pop culture juggernaut that it was in the 2010s. Still, this doesn't diminish the quality of Telltale's The Walking Dead - it's still an absolute must-play for anyone who likes this kind of game (and even for most who don't). In terms of new TWD games, there's not much happening at the moment. A side-scrolling action brawler named The Walking Dead: Streets of Survival launches later this month, which should give gamers another excuse to return to the universe if they can't get their hands on a free Steam key for Telltale's game.
